newsitem.title: USA: Nassau County, NY, fights planned methadone clinic.
newsitem.headline: Nassau County, NY, fights planned methadone clinic.

text.p: Nassau County, N.Y., on Wednesday pledged to do whatever was needed to block the state from setting up a methadone clinic in the middle of Hempstead, saying it would derail efforts to keep the area growing.

Nassau County Executive Thomas Gulotta said: "The placement of an unneeded and unnecessary 700-patient methadone clinic in the heart of the village would deal a fatal blow to our efforts to maintain Hempstead's revitalization. We cannot and will not permit that to happen," according to a prepared statement.

Hempstead Mayor James Garner joined the county executive in his opposition to the plan, which would put the new clinic at the former bus terminal, a location they said was in the heart of the town's shopping district.

The officials said that there was no waiting list for methadone treatment in Nassau, adding that the network of agencies serving the county had never said they needed more programs, and no historic or current data justified such an expansion. They also noted the four existing treatment programs were based in hospitals.
